records.source_span: I'm wearing a Garmin Fenix 7X Sapphire Solar, the 51mm version. I got it around early March
I gave the Apple Watch Series 8 to my sister at the end of February
I switched to the SolarFace watch face from Connect IQ. I like the minimal look — just time, date, battery, and steps.
records.value: SolarFace with time, date, battery, steps only

records.source_span: I tried one of those data-heavy faces with like six complications crammed in and I took it off after a single day
I turned off almost all phone notifications on the Garmin. I just want it to tell me the time and track my body — I don't need another screen nagging me. The only thing I left on is phone calls
records.value: phone calls only; all other notifications disabled

records.source_span: I picked up a Garmin HRM-Pro Plus chest strap from REI for $129.99 and I've been using it on my Tuesday and Thursday morning runs

records.source_span: My resting heart rate has been averaging about 58 bpm, which my doctor said was good at my checkup on April 22nd

records.source_span: I was thinking about how my Garmin handles solar charging during long outdoor days

records.source_span: I want a hiking profile that shows elapsed time, distance, elevation gain, and heart rate — but only during the activity. On the main watch face day-to-day, I still just want SolarFace with the four fields.
records.value: hiking profile with elapsed time, distance, elevation gain, heart rate; daily face remains minimal

records.source_span: when it comes to anything on my wrist, I just want it to be as invisible as possible. Show me what matters, nothing else. Like a good tool should just work and get out of the way.
records.value: wearable tech should be invisible and unobtrusive; tool-first mindset

records.source_span: The battery barely moved even with GPS tracking the whole time. That reliability is part of the same thing — I don't want to worry about charging.
records.value: battery reliability and long-term endurance without frequent charging

records.source_span: the always-on transflective display was a huge deal for me. I hated how my old Apple Watch screen would go dark and I'd have to flick my wrist just to see the time. With the Garmin, the screen is just always there, readable in sunlight without any backlight.
records.value: always-on transflective display; readable in sunlight without backlight
